### AWS DVA-C02 — AWS Certified Developer Associate (DVA-C02) Practice Exams
- Study Guide: https://gabhack.github.io/cloudcert-lab/exams/aws-dva-c02/
- Free Interactive Simulator (15 Qs): https://gabhack.github.io/cloudcert-lab/?exam=aws-dva-c02&mode=study
- Free Flashcards: https://gabhack.github.io/cloudcert-lab/?exam=aws-dva-c02&mode=flashcards
- Official Udemy Course (260 Qs · $49.99): https://www.udemy.com/course/aws-certified-developer-associate-dva-c02-practice-exams-dx/
- Companion Amazon Book: https://www.amazon.com/author/gabrieln (AWS Associate Series · Free on Kindle Unlimited)
- Exam Format: 130 minutes · Passing Bar 72% · 4 Full 65-Q Mocks (260 Pro Qs)
- Blueprint Domains:
  - Domain 1: Development with AWS Services
  - Domain 2: Security
  - Domain 3: Deployment
  - Domain 4: Troubleshooting and Optimization
- Verified Exam Hacks:
  - Eliminate Lambda cold starts = Provisioned Concurrency (or SnapStart for Java) on a Version/Alias. Cap a function so it doesn't overwhelm a downstream RDS DB = Reserved Concurrency. Share common SDKs/certs across functions = Lambda Layers.
  - Multiple consumers needing real-time replay + ordering per PartitionKey = Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Use Enhanced Fan-Out when multiple consumers need dedicated 2 MB/s read bandwidth without throttling.
  - DynamoDB Golden Math: 1 RCU = 4 KB Strong (or 2x4 KB Eventual); 1 WCU = 1 KB. Add new Partition Key query pattern on existing table = GSI (Eventual reads only). Microsecond read cache for hot keys = DAX.

## 2. Comparison & Migration Guides (2026–2027)

### AWS DVA-C02 vs DVA-C03 (Dec 2026): Complete Exam Blueprint & Migration Guide
- URL: https://gabhack.github.io/cloudcert-lab/exams/aws-dva-c02-vs-dva-c03/

  - **Take DVA-C02 if:** Your exam appointment is already booked before November 30, 2026 and your preparation focuses purely on classic Lambda, DynamoDB, SAM, CodePipeline, and X-Ray.
  - **Take DVA-C03 if:** You are testing on or after December 1, 2026, or want future-proof mastery of Amazon Q Developer, Bedrock Guardrails, dependency slopsquatting defense, and modern AWS testing pipelines.

  - **Start with AWS AIF-C01 if:** You build or govern solutions on AWS and need deep command of Amazon Bedrock, Knowledge Bases for RAG, Guardrails, SageMaker AI, and IAM/KMS compliance.
  - **Start with GCP GenAI Leader if:** You lead product, strategy, or enterprise transformation on Google Workspace / Vertex AI and want mastery of Gemini, Grounding with Google Search, and Agentspace.

## 3. Cloud & AI Exam Traps Glossary (12 Core Distinctions)

- **Amazon Bedrock Guardrails vs AWS IAM (AWS AIF-C01 / DVA-C03):** AWS IAM controls who can invoke Amazon Bedrock APIs at the infrastructure level, whereas Amazon Bedrock Guardrails inspects prompts and model outputs at runtime to block PII leakage, hallucinations (contextual grounding), prompt injection, and denied topics. *Exam Trap: Pick IAM for API access control; pick Bedrock Guardrails for content safety, PII redaction, or topic filtering.*
- **RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) vs Fine-Tuning (AWS AIF-C01 / Azure AI-901 / GCP GenAI):** RAG injects fresh, verifiable private documents into the prompt at inference time via a vector store (Bedrock Knowledge Bases, Azure AI Search, Vertex AI Search) without modifying model weights, while fine-tuning updates weights to teach domain style, tone, or strict output formatting. *Exam Trap: Whenever a scenario mentions frequently changing data, citations, or lowest training cost, RAG beats fine-tuning.*
- **Microsoft Foundry Hub vs Project (Azure AI-901) (Azure AI-901):** In Microsoft Foundry, a Hub provides top-level enterprise governance, shared networking, Entra ID security, and Key Vault configuration, while individual Projects isolate workloads, datasets, prompt flows, and model endpoints for separate engineering teams. *Exam Trap: Share governance at the Hub level; isolate team workspaces and billing/RBAC inside separate Projects.*
- **Slopsquatting & AI Package Hallucination Defense (AWS DVA-C03) (AWS DVA-C03 (New Dec 2026)):** Slopsquatting occurs when attackers register non-existent package names repeatedly hallucinated by AI coding assistants on npm or PyPI. On AWS DVA-C03, teams defend against this using AWS CodeArtifact private upstream repositories, dependency lockfiles, and automated SCA scanning in CI/CD. *Exam Trap: Route all developer installs through AWS CodeArtifact with verified lockfiles rather than unrestricted public registries.*
- **AWS Lambda SnapStart vs Provisioned Concurrency (AWS DVA-C03 / DVA-C02):** Lambda SnapStart snapshots and caches the initialized execution environment (Firecracker microVM) for Java, Python, and .NET functions to slash cold starts by up to 90% at zero extra cost, whereas Provisioned Concurrency keeps warm containers running continuously for a fixed hourly fee. *Exam Trap: Choose SnapStart for cost-effective cold-start reduction on supported runtimes; choose Provisioned Concurrency only when strict sub-100ms tail latency or unsupported runtimes require it.*
- **Google Cloud Grounding with Google Search vs Enterprise Data (GCP GenAI Leader):** Grounding with Google Search anchors Gemini responses to live public web facts with inline citations, while Grounding with Vertex AI Search connects models to private enterprise PDFs, databases, and Drive files under IAM access controls. *Exam Trap: Use Google Search grounding for real-time public events; use Vertex AI Search grounding for internal policies or customer data.*
- **Amazon S3 Tables & Apache Iceberg (AWS DEA-C01) (AWS DEA-C01):** Amazon S3 Tables provides native managed storage optimized for Apache Iceberg tabular data with automated compaction, snapshot management, and ACID transactions—eliminating manual small-file maintenance on S3 data lakes. *Exam Trap: When a DEA-C01 scenario asks for ACID upserts, time-travel queries, and automated compaction on S3 with minimal ops, pick S3 Tables / Apache Iceberg.*
- **SageMaker Model Monitor vs SageMaker Clarify (AWS MLA-C01) (AWS MLA-C01):** Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor continuously detects data drift, concept drift, and model quality degradation on live production endpoints, whereas SageMaker Clarify measures pre-training/post-training bias and computes SHAP feature explainability. *Exam Trap: Drift alerts in production = Model Monitor; fairness, demographic bias, or SHAP feature attribution = Clarify.*
- **VPC Gateway Endpoint vs VPC Interface Endpoint (AWS SAA-C03) (AWS SAA-C03):** A VPC Gateway Endpoint routes private traffic to Amazon S3 and DynamoDB via route table entries at $0 per hour and $0 data processing cost, while an Interface Endpoint (AWS PrivateLink) uses an ENI with private IP and hourly charges for 100+ other AWS services. *Exam Trap: For S3 or DynamoDB inside a VPC, always choose a Gateway Endpoint first for the lowest cost unless on-premises VPN/Direct Connect access requires an Interface Endpoint.*
- **AWS Shared Responsibility Model (CLF-C02) (AWS CLF-C02):** AWS is responsible for Security OF the Cloud (physical data centers, hardware, virtualization hypervisor, and managed service layers), while the customer is responsible for Security IN the Cloud (customer data encryption, IAM policies, security groups, and guest OS patching on EC2). *Exam Trap: Patching an EC2 guest OS = Customer; patching RDS/Lambda underlying OS = AWS; IAM users & S3 bucket policies = Customer.*
- **DynamoDB GSI (Global Secondary Index) vs LSI (Local Secondary Index) (AWS DVA-C03 / DVA-C02):** A Global Secondary Index (GSI) can be created or deleted anytime with a different partition key and independent throughput (eventual consistency only), whereas a Local Secondary Index (LSI) must be defined at table creation, shares the base partition key, and supports strongly consistent reads. *Exam Trap: Existing table needing a new query pattern = GSI; strongly consistent alternate sort key on a new table = LSI.*
- **Amazon Bedrock Converse API vs InvokeModel (AWS AIP-C01 / DVA-C03) (AWS DVA-C03 / AIP-C01):** The Bedrock Converse API provides a single unified request/response schema (including tool use, system prompts, and Guardrails) across Claude, Llama, Nova, and Mistral models, removing model-specific JSON payload rewrites required by raw InvokeModel calls. *Exam Trap: Whenever a question emphasizes portable multi-model switching or standardized tool calling on Bedrock, choose the Converse API.*

## 4. 2026–2027 Cloud & AI Certification Costs, Passing Scores & Retake Fees
- URL: https://gabhack.github.io/cloudcert-lab/exams/cloud-ai-exam-costs-passing-scores-2026/
- **Foundational Exams ($99–$100 USD · 70% Pass Bar · 90 min):** Microsoft Azure AI-901 ($99), Google Cloud Generative AI Leader ($99), AWS CLF-C02 ($100), AWS AIF-C01 ($100).
- **AWS Associate Exams ($150 USD · 72% Pass Bar · 130 min · 65 Qs):** AWS DVA-C03 (effective Dec 1, 2026), AWS DVA-C02, AWS SAA-C03, AWS DEA-C01, AWS MLA-C01. Passing a Foundational AWS exam grants a 50% voucher ($75 Associate / $150 Pro).
- **AWS Professional Exams ($300 USD · 75% Pass Bar · 170 min · 75 Qs):** AWS Generative AI Developer Pro (AIP-C01).
- **Retake Wait Policies:** AWS enforces a 14-day wait after any fail; Azure requires 24 hours after first fail (14 days after 2nd+); Google Cloud requires 14 days after 1st fail and 60 days after 2nd fail. None provide free retakes.
